title: Bank Account Simulator
story: Open an account with $0. Deposit your paycheck. Withdraw for rent. Transfer to savings. Earn interest. Every transaction is verified by contracts: balance never goes negative, transfers require sufficient funds, interest only on positive balances. This is banking with mathematical certainty.
why: The bank simulator demonstrates contracts (requires/ensures/invariant) on real-world domain logic — financial transactions where correctness is non-negotiable.
analogy: A bank vault with a meticulous teller who checks ID (requires), counts money twice (ensures), and never lets an account go negative (invariant). Every deposit, withdrawal, and transfer is logged in the ledger (transaction history). The contracts are the bank's security cameras — they never blink.
try_it: Add a fee system: $5 per withdrawal after the 3rd withdrawal per month. Implement a savings account variant with higher interest but withdrawal limits. Add joint accounts where two owners can both deposit/withdraw. Try withdraw(500) on an account with 200 — contract fires!
tips: Requires on withdraw/transfer ensure sufficient funds BEFORE the operation
Transactions should be atomic — either both accounts update or neither
common_mistakes: Allowing withdrawal without checking balance — contract should REQUIRE sufficient funds
Applying interest to negative balances — should be only on positive balance
Transfer subtracting from one account but not adding to the other — missing the second update
